## Example 1.4 · Other bases {#dc1-example-1-4 .dc-lesson}

<div class="dc-result"><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}(a^x)=(\ln a)a^x\qquad(a>0)"></span></div>
<p>Differentiate the following functions:</p>
<div class="dc-problem-list"><div><span class="part">a)</span><span data-math="y=2^x"></span></div><div><span class="part">b)</span><span data-math="y=5\left(\frac13\right)^x"></span></div></div><p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 4 · Example 1.4(a–b)</p>

::: notes
Before part (b), ask: “Should the derivative be positive or negative? Explain.” This brief prediction connects a base between zero and one to decreasing exponential values. (a) y'=(ln 2)2^x. (b) y'=5 ln(1/3)(1/3)^x=-5 ln 3 (1/3)^x. Keep logarithms exact. Explain why ln(1/3)=-ln3. Do not change the base to 1/5 or move the coefficient 5 into the exponent. About three minutes.
:::
